TemplateCache log lines expose entry count only ('size=<n> entries, evictions=<n>'), never bytes or bytes-per-entry; and memory_pct has no absolute-byte denominator (pod limit unknown), so (RSS_new_gen_bytes)/(entry_count) cannot be computed as an absolute ratio.

The 03-21 memory_pct window query (tc-047, 2026-03-21T16:45-23:10Z) timed out after 3 attempts, so I could not bracket the 03-21 196650-entry point with a matching memory value at the same granularity used for 03-22/03-23.

events.answer: A true heap attribution (bytes held by TemplateCache vs all other live objects) is NOT obtainable: notification-service exposes only 7 metrics (consumer_lag, cpu_pct, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts) — no heap/old-gen/class-histogram metric exists, memory_pct is a percentage with no absolute byte denominator, and the TemplateCache log lines carry only entry counts, no byte sizes. What the available evidence does show: TemplateCache entry count tracks the memory ramp almost linearly across all three cycles, and the bytes-per-entry ratio is NOT constant — at the 03-23 ~94% point 188100 entries coincide with 93.86% memory while 03-21/03-22 hit ~92-95% with 196650 entries, i.e. fewer entries at equal-or-higher memory on 03-23. The cache grows unboundedly with evictions=0 and resets only at restart, consistent with the cache being a large/dominant contributor (H1), but the data cannot exclude a co-resident non-cache leak (H5) nor prove the cache holds a majority of live heap bytes.

events.title: notification-service v3.8.0's unbounded in-memory TemplateCache leaks heap and OOMs the pod
Chronic pre-existing memory growth / underprovisioned heap, with the cache as accelerator not origin
A memory-limit/quota reduction (config change) narrowed headroom, making a normal cache footprint OOM
An upstream producer or the external email-provider degraded, causing message accumulation in notification-service
Kafka maintenance (retention reduction) triggered a consumer replay that notification-service buffered in memory

events.summary: H1 (unbounded in-memory TemplateCache in notification-service v3.8.0 leaking heap to OOMKill) is the best-supported and adequately grounded hypothesis after three rounds. Mechanism: the cache never evicts (evictions=0 on every log line, F14/F34) and its entry count grows monotonically ~50k→~190-197k within each cycle, resetting exactly at each restart in lockstep with the container memory sawtooth (F8/F9/F14/F15/F34); saturation produces escalating old-gen full-GC WARNs terminating in kubelet exit-137 OOMKills (F10/F13/F18/F26). The near-daily ~23h periodicity spans 03-21/03-22/03-23 and predates and is independent of the 18:00Z Kafka maintenance (F7/F26). Alternatives are actively contradicted by verified findings: H2/H4 (Kafka replay / upstream) by the absence of any replay/rebalance/deserialization error and by lag spikes coinciding with rather than preceding the OOM (F11/F12/F13/F17/F18); H3 (limit reduction) by the absence of any config change touching notification-service limits/consumer settings and by the gradual ramp rather than an abrupt new ceiling (F2/F4/F8/F9); H5 (pre-existing non-cache leak / underprovisioned heap) by the flat pre-deploy baseline day with zero restarts and the lockstep cache↔memory reset, and it identifies no alternative source (F28/F29/F33/F36). Cross-service exclusivity is verified: auth/order/settlement remain flat at ~49-60% with zero restarts, excluding an infra/node-wide cause (F19-F24). Two residual uncertainties do NOT name a different origin and therefore do not block acceptance: (a) the pre-deploy onset span (03-01..03-19) is confirmed unrecoverable (F25/F30), so 'first-ever OOM' cannot be bounded; and (b) byte-level heap attribution to the cache is unmeasurable because no heap/class/old-gen-bytes metric exists (F31/F32/F35), leaving the cache's majority-of-heap claim as correlation, with the non-constant entry-count/memory ratio (F33/F36) as mild counter-evidence. These are secondary-detail uncertainties of an established mechanism, handled via the confidence cap and stated assumptions rather than further evidence. The third-round discriminator I requested (heap attribution) was attempted and is confirmed permanently unobtainable, so no obtainable evidence remains that could change the ranking.

critiques.summary: H1 (unbounded in-memory TemplateCache in notification-service v3.8.0 leaking heap to OOMKill) is the best-supported and adequately grounded hypothesis after three rounds. Mechanism: the cache never evicts (evictions=0 on every log line, F14/F34) and its entry count grows monotonically ~50k→~190-197k within each cycle, resetting exactly at each restart in lockstep with the container memory sawtooth (F8/F9/F14/F15/F34); saturation produces escalating old-gen full-GC WARNs terminating in kubelet exit-137 OOMKills (F10/F13/F18/F26). Cross-service exclusivity is verified: auth/order/settlement remain flat at ~49-60% with zero restarts, excluding an infra/node-wide cause (F19-F24). Two residual uncertainties do NOT name a different origin and therefore do not block acceptance: (a) the pre-deploy onset span (03-01..03-19) is confirmed unrecoverable (F25/F30), so 'first-ever OOM' cannot be bounded; and (b) byte-level heap attribution to the cache is unmeasurable because no heap/class/old-gen-bytes metric exists (F31/F32/F35), leaving the cache's majority-of-heap claim as correlation, with the non-constant entry-count/memory ratio (F33/F36) as mild counter-evidence. These are secondary-detail uncertainties of an established mechanism, handled via the confidence cap and stated assumptions rather than further evidence. The third-round discriminator I requested (heap attribution) was attempted and is confirmed permanently unobtainable, so no obtainable evidence remains that could change the ranking.

challenges.issue: Heap attribution to the TemplateCache is correlation, not measured: no per-class/old-gen-bytes metric exists (F31/F32/F35), so 'cache is the dominant heap consumer' is unproven.
